newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr up vs yen, boosted by mark/yen rise in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr up vs yen, boosted by mark/yen rise in Tokyo.

text.p: 0011 GMT--*Dollar edged higher against yen in early Tokyo, buoyed by a rise in mark/yen rate.

*Traders keen to cover mark short positions in wake of overnight comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that dollar's recovery against mark from historic lows in 1995 was complete, dealers said.
*Mark/yen stood at 64.80/83 yen at 0011 GMT against 64.60 yen in late New York on Thursday.
*But dollar's rise capped near 113.50 yen by exporter offers for now.
*A dealer at a long-term credit bank said mark/yen could rise further if stop-loss buying is triggered at 64.80-90 yen.

*"Dollar offers are expected at around 113.50 yen. But if greenback clearly break through that point, triggering possible stop-loss purchases, it could rise towards 113.80 and then 114 yen," a trust bank dealer said.

*Mark pared recent losses overnight after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said central bank was watching foreign exchange developments closely and believed dollar/mark was now "in a phase in which the (post-1995) correction has clearly come to an end".
